skill.displayName: Nano Banana Pro 精准文字图片

llm.summary: The skill appears intended for AI Hive image generation, but its activation text is much broader than its actual purpose and could route unrelated searches into a paid remote workflow.

dimensions.detail: Network calls, selected local file uploads, task polling, and downloads to ~/Downloads/AiHive are expected for remote image generation, but users should understand prompts and reference files are sent to AI Hive.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation requires Python requests, and initialization opens the AI Hive page and writes an API key to a local config file; this is disclosed and user-driven.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill description and documentation include extensive competitor, marketplace, platform, pricing, API, and search-intent keywords, making invocation materially broader than explicit requests to generate or edit images with this service.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill stores an API key in ~/.ai-hive/config.json with 0600 permissions and also supports API keys via environment variable or command-line argument; no background persistence or privilege escalation was found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The active skill entry point supports image generation, task lookup, image/media upload, and API-key initialization for AI Hive, which mostly fits the stated Nano Banana Pro image-generation purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this before installing if you only want a narrowly triggered Nano Banana Pro image tool. Use it only for content you are allowed to send to AI Hive, confirm costs before batch generation, prefer the 0600 config file or environment variable over command-line secrets, and avoid invoking it for generic tool comparisons or pricing research unless you explicitly want this service involved.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: Network access, selected file reads/uploads, output writes, and environment/config lookup are consistent with the AI Hive image-generation workflow, though an explicit permissions summary would improve transparency.
[TP4] unexpected: The script contains generic AI Hive helper code for chat, video, user info, and model listing, but the active __main__ path uses the skill-specific parser exposing generate, task, upload, and init only, so this was downgraded from a direct capability mismatch.
[SQP-1] unexpected: The frontmatter trigger text is overbroad and includes many competitors, ecommerce platforms, and comparison/search intents beyond explicit Nano Banana Pro image-generation requests.
[SQP-1] unexpected: The body repeats broad search and migration coverage, which creates a real scoping concern because the skill can use an API key, upload user-selected media, and submit paid remote tasks.
[SQP-2] expected: Uploading reference images and sending prompts to AI Hive is inherent to the stated workflow and is described in the data flow, but the privacy implication is not highlighted prominently.
[SQP-2] expected: Local API-key storage is disclosed and chmodded to 0600; accepting --api-key on the command line is convenient but should be used carefully because shell history or process listings may expose secrets.
